chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Rayyan narrated to me, saying: Ubaidullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan al-Wasiti narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Kufi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him).

He said: I said: May I be sacrificed for you, there is a narration that Abdullah ibn Bukair used to narrate, from Ubaid ibn Zurara. He said: Then he said to me: And what is it? I said: It was narrated from Ubaid ibn Zurara that he met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the year Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Hasan went out (in opposition), and he said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, indeed this man has made his speech friendly and the people hastened to him, so what do you command?

He said: Then he said: Fear Allah and be calm as long as the Heaven and the earth are calm. He said: Abdullah ibn Bukair used to say: By Allah, if Ubaid ibn Zurara was truthful, then there will be no going out (for opposition) nor any Riser.

He said: Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: The narration is according to what Ubaid narrated, and not according to what Abdullah ibn Bukair interpreted. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) only meant by his saying: 'as long as the Heaven is calm' the call with the name of your leader, and 'as long as the earth is calm' the sinking of the army.

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Ibrahim ibn Abdillah, a leader who led an uprising against the Abbasids
key_terms.الْخَسْف: The sinking or swallowing of the army, a sign associated with the Mahdi
key_terms.صَاحِبُكَ: Your leader, referring to the Imam or the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'as long as the Heaven and the earth are calm' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) refutes Abdullah ibn Bukair’s interpretation that the phrase signifies a period of inactivity, clarifying instead that the 'calmness of the heavens' refers to the proclamation of the Imam’s name and the 'calmness of the earth' to the divine punishment (khasf) of his army. This distinction underscores the active, imminent nature of the Qiyam, where cosmic signs accompany the establishment of justice rather than indicating a delay in the uprising.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, that he said: We were told by Sahl bin Ziyad, that he said: I was told by Ali bin Raiyan, that he said: We were told by Ubaidullah bin Abdullah al-Dahqan al-Wasiti, from Hussain bin Khalid al-Kufi, from Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him,

that he said: I said: May I be sacrificed for you. There is a narration that was narrated by Abdullah bin Bukair, ofUbaid bin Zurara. He said: Then he said: And what is it? He said: I said: It was narrated from Ubaid bin Zurara, that he met Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, in the year Ibrahim bin Abdullah ibn Hasan went out (in opposition), and that he said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, indeed, this man has made his speech friendly and made the people quickly join him, so what do you command (us) to?

He said: Then he said: Fear Allah and be calm as long as the Heaven and the earth are calm. He said: Abdullah bin Bukair also used to say: By Allah, verily, if Ubaid bin Zurara was truthful, there will be no going out (for opposition), nor any Riser.

He said: Then Abu’l-Hasan, peace be upon him, said to me: The narration is according to what Ubaid narrated, and not according to what Abdullah bin Bukair interpreted. Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, only meant with his saying: «as long as the Heaven is calm» for the call with the name of your man, and with «as long as the earth is clam» for the army to sink.
